errorRules.message: Wafer returned HTTP 401 authentication_error. Check {apiKeyEnvVar}. Get one at {setupUrl}

instructions: 1. Visit: https://app.wafer.ai and sign in — the docs say "Sign in at app.wafer.ai to add credits and create an API key. Store your key securely." (https://docs.wafer.ai/serverless)
2. Add credits and create an API key — the docs say "Add credits, create an API key, and pay per token." (https://docs.wafer.ai/serverless)
3. Set {apiKeyEnvVar} in your .env file (the docs' Authentication row shows the Authorization: Bearer header)
setup.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://pass.wafer.ai/v1 (https://docs.wafer.ai/serverless: "Access Wafer models through an OpenAI-compatible API."), with the 8 models the unauthenticated GET /models roster listed on 2026-09-29 in models.catalog. An unauthenticated GET of https://pass.wafer.ai/v1/chat/completions returned HTTP 401 with error.type authentication_error and error.code missing_api_key (2026-09-29), so errorRules match status 401. models.defaultContextWindow (128000) and models.defaultMaxOutputTokens (16384) are placeholders the vendor does not publish. billingPolicy is recorded as no-free-tier because the schema has no unknown value; the vendor's stated flow is "Add credits, create an API key, and pay per token."
